newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Client demand, short cover boost India.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Client demand, short cover boost India.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) rallied on Monday amid strong client demand and as short sellers were forced to turn buyers.

"There was some client demand out there on the back of strength in the local market but there was also a squeeze from traders and the real level of demand was not as comprehensive as the jump suggested," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed up 2.87 points, or 4.64 percent, at 64.75 points, with the premium over the local market expanding to 18.77 percent from Friday's 13.71 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index closed up 32.57 points, or 1.04 percent, at 3,171.59.
"The local market will open up around 60 points on Tuesday," forecast a trader.
Hindalco GDRs rallied 45 cents to $18.75/$19.75, after the company's first half net profit fell 2.5 percent to 2.03 billion rupees from the previous year.
"Hindalco's results probably dampened expectations for the stock, usually when the market is rising, Hindalco is one name up there, but that was not true to the same extent today," said a trader.
Century Textiles GDR fell $6.00 to $58.00/$73.00 after it reported a 67 percent fall in net profit to 341.8 million rupees from 1.02 billion rupees.
Indian Rayon's net profit climbed 11 percent to 998.4 million rupees. The GDR responded with a 40 cent rise to $7.00/$8.00.
"Century's earnings definitely had an impact on the stock, Indian Rayon less so because the stock has been under pressure for some time," said the trader.
Traders also noted strong client demand for Ranbaxy, up 71 cents $19.25/$20.25, and Telco, up 50 cents to $12.25/$13.25.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.32 points up, or 2.00 percent, at 67.52, a premium of 29.06 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index closed at 750.82, down 5.85 points from the previous close.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 1.51 points higher, or 1.67 percent, at 91.77, a premium of 1.97 percent after the Taiwan Weighted index rose 63.62 points, or 0.96 percent, to 6,659.72.
